question: The manager, along with his team members, were praised for completing the project on time. Identify the incorrect part.

options.D: for completing the project on time

explanation: Rule 1: Phrases such as 'along with', 'together with', and 'as well as' do not change the number of the main subject.
Rule 2: The main subject 'manager' is singular.
Application: The singular subject requires 'was praised'.
Correct sentence: The manager, along with his team members, was praised for completing the project on time.

question: Not only the coach but also the players was celebrating their victory after the final match. Identify the incorrect part.

options.D: their victory after the final match

explanation: Rule 1: With 'not only...but also', the verb generally agrees with the subject closest to it.
Rule 2: The nearest subject is 'players', which is plural.
Application: The plural subject requires 'were celebrating'.
Correct sentence: Not only the coach but also the players were celebrating their victory after the final match.

question: Each of the participants in the singing competition have been awarded a certificate. Identify the incorrect part.

explanation: Rule 1: 'Each of' takes a singular verb in formal subject-verb agreement.
Rule 2: The main subject is 'each', not 'participants'.
Application: The singular subject requires 'has been awarded'.
Correct sentence: Each of the participants in the singing competition has been awarded a certificate.

question: Neither of the two books contain the information required for our science project. Identify the incorrect part.

explanation: Rule 1: 'Neither' used as a pronoun is treated as singular in formal English.
Rule 2: The phrase 'of the two books' does not change the number of the subject.
Application: The singular subject requires 'contains'.
Correct sentence: Neither of the two books contains the information required for our science project.

question: Either of the top chefs cook the signature dish on weekends, but the assistant chefs cooks the side items. Identify the parts containing errors.

options.A: Either of the top chefs cook

explanation: Rule 1: 'Either of + plural noun' takes a singular verb in formal English.
Rule 2: 'Either of the top chefs' requires 'cooks'.
Rule 3: The plural subject 'assistant chefs' requires the plural verb 'cook'.
Application: Correct both verbs: 'cook' becomes 'cooks', and 'cooks' becomes 'cook'.
Correct sentence: Either of the top chefs cooks the signature dish on weekends, but the assistant chefs cook the side items.

question: Everybody in the meeting room were asked to turn off their mobile phones. Identify the incorrect part.

options.D: to turn off their mobile phones

explanation: Rule 1: Indefinite pronouns such as 'everybody', 'everyone', and 'someone' take singular verbs.
Rule 2: The subject 'everybody' is grammatically singular.
Application: The singular subject requires 'was asked'.
Correct sentence: Everybody in the meeting room was asked to turn off their mobile phones.

question: A lot of information about the upcoming board examinations were provided on the website. Identify the incorrect part.

explanation: Rule 1: 'A lot of' takes a verb that agrees with the noun following 'of'.
Rule 2: 'Information' is an uncountable singular noun.
Application: The singular noun requires 'was provided'.
Correct sentence: A lot of information about the upcoming board examinations was provided on the website.

question: There is a few time left before the exam begins, so revise your notes quickly. Identify the incorrect part.

explanation: Rule 1: 'A few' is used with countable plural nouns.
Rule 2: 'Time' is uncountable when referring to an amount of time.
Application: Use 'a little time' for an uncountable noun.
Correct sentence: There is a little time left before the exam begins, so revise your notes quickly.

question: The poor is facing many difficulties due to the unexpected rise in basic daily expenses. Identify the incorrect part.

options.D: due to the unexpected rise in basic daily expenses

explanation: Rule 1: 'The + adjective' can refer to a group of people as a whole.
Rule 2: 'The poor' refers to poor people and takes a plural verb.
Application: The plural subject requires 'are facing'.
Correct sentence: The poor are facing many difficulties due to the unexpected rise in basic daily expenses.

question: Aman is one of those smart students who answers every difficult question correctly. Identify the incorrect part.

explanation: Rule 1: In 'one of those + plural noun + who', the relative pronoun 'who' generally refers to the plural noun.
Rule 2: Here, 'who' refers to 'students', which is plural.
Application: The plural subject requires 'answer'.
Correct sentence: Aman is one of those smart students who answer every difficult question correctly.
